title: Time: あとで, までに, とき, ながら & おきに
description: After, by (a deadline), when (and the tense trap 行くとき vs 行ったとき), while doing, and 'every other'.

points.title: 〜あとで: after
points.summary: た-form + あとで / noun + の + あとで = 'after …'. The verb before あとで is always past (た).
points.body:
**Formation:**
- Verb: **た-form** + あとで: 食べ**た**あとで, 勉強し**た**あとで
- Noun: noun + **の** + あとで: 授業**の**あとで

The verb is always in the た-form, even when the main sentence is about the future: 明日、仕事が終わ**った**あとで電話します.

**あとで vs あとに:** both mean 'after'. あとで focuses on *where in the sequence* the action happens; あとに is used more for one-off events and in writing. At N4, あとで is the safe default.

**あとで vs てから:** てから stresses the **order** ('only after A, then B'); あとで is a simple 'after'.

Alone, **あとで** = 'later': あとで電話します.
examples: ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べたあとで、{散歩|さんぽ}します。
I'll take a walk after eating.
{授業|じゅぎょう}のあとで、{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}きます。
I'll go to the library after class.

points.title: 〜までに: by (deadline)
points.summary: Time / dictionary form + までに = 'by …, no later than …'. For one-time actions with a deadline — not for continuing actions (that's まで).
points.body:
**Formation:**
- Time noun + までに: 金曜日**までに**, 5時**までに**
- Verb (dictionary form) + までに: 母が帰る**までに** (by the time mother gets back)

**までに vs まで** (very common test point):
- **までに** → a single action that must happen *before* the deadline: レポートを金曜日**までに**出す.
- **まで** → an action or state that *continues up to* that point: 5時**まで**働く.

Quick test: 'by' → までに; 'until' → まで.
examples: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}までにメールを{送|おく}ってください。
Please send the email by tomorrow morning.
{母|はは}が{帰|かえ}るまでに、{部屋|へや}を{片付|かたづ}けます。
I'll tidy my room before (by the time) my mother comes home.

points.title: 〜とき: when, at the time
points.summary: Plain form / な-adj + な / noun + の + とき = 'when …'. The tense inside the とき-clause shows whether A happens before or after B.
points.body:
**Formation:**
- Verb: plain form: 行く**とき**, 行った**とき**
- い-adjective: 寒い**とき**
- な-adjective: 暇**な**とき
- Noun: 子供**の**とき

**The tense trap (N4 favourite):** the verb before とき is about the timing *relative to the main action*:
- **行くとき** = when (on the way / before) going → the main action happens **before arriving**: 日本へ**行く**とき、空港でカメラを買った (bought it at the airport before leaving).
- **行ったとき** = when (after) having gone → the main action happens **there, after arriving**: 日本へ**行った**とき、富士山に登った.

Same with 寝る/寝たとき, 来る/来たとき, etc.
examples: {日本|にほん}へ{行|い}くとき、{空港|くうこう}でカメラを{買|か}いました。
When I was going to Japan, I bought a camera at the airport (before leaving).
{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}ったとき、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りました。
When I went to Japan, I climbed Mt. Fuji (there).
{暇|ひま}なとき、{何|なに}をしますか。
What do you do when you're free?

points.title: 〜ながら: while (doing)
points.summary: ます-stem + ながら + main verb = doing two things at the same time. Same subject; the main action comes last.
points.body:
**Formation:** ます-stem + ながら: 聞き**ながら**, 食べ**ながら**, し**ながら**.

**Rules:**
- **One subject** does both actions. ✗ 私が歌いながら、妹がピアノを弾く (two people → use 間に / とき).
- The **main** action is the second one: 音楽を聞きながら勉強する = 'studying (main) while listening to music'.
- Tense and politeness are carried by the final verb.

(At N3 you'll meet ながら(も) = 'although': 狭いながらも楽しい家.)
examples: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}きながら{勉強|べんきょう}します。
I study while listening to music.
{歩|ある}きながらスマホを{見|み}ないでください。
Please don't look at your phone while walking.

points.title: 〜おきに: every (other), at intervals of
points.summary: Number + counter + おきに = at intervals of …. With days, 一日おき = every other day (one day skipped).
points.body:
**Formation:** quantity + **おきに**: 10分**おきに**, 2メートル**おきに**, 一日**おきに**.

**Meaning:** something repeats with a gap of that size.
- 10分おきにバスが来る → a bus every 10 minutes.
- **一日おき** → every **other** day (Mon, Wed, Fri …): one full day is skipped in between.

**おきに vs ごとに:** for days/weeks they differ — 一日**ごとに** = every single day, 一日**おきに** = every other day. For minutes/hours both usually mean the same.

Don't confuse with **ずつ** ('each, per'): 一人に三つ**ずつ** (three each).
examples: このバスは10{分|ぷん}おきに{来|き}ます。
This bus comes every 10 minutes.
{一日|いちにち}おきに{運動|うんどう}しています。
I exercise every other day.

questions.prompt: ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べた（　）、{散歩|さんぽ}します。
notes: まえに needs the dictionary form (食べるまえに).
までに follows the dictionary form or a noun, not the た-form.
ながら needs the ます-stem (食べながら).
questions.translation: I'll take a walk after eating.

questions.prompt: ご{飯|はん}を（　）あとで、{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
questions.explanation: The verb before あとで is always the **た-form**.
notes: The dictionary form goes with まえに, not あとで.
The ます-stem can't come before あとで.
The て-form can't come before あとで.
questions.translation: I brush my teeth after eating.

questions.prompt: {授業|じゅぎょう}（　）あとで、{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}きます。
notes: 授業があとで isn't grammatical.
な is for な-adjectives, not nouns.
授業をあとで would mean 'postpone class until later'.
questions.translation: I'll go to the library after class.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}（　）メールを{送|おく}ってください。
questions.explanation: Deadline for a one-time action → **までに**.
notes: からに isn't a form.
まで = keep sending until tomorrow morning — sending is a one-time action.
までと isn't a deadline pattern.
questions.translation: Please send the email by tomorrow morning.

questions.prompt: {金曜日|きんようび}（　）に{返事|へんじ}をください。
questions.explanation: 金曜日**までに** = by Friday.
notes: Nouns need の before あと, and 'after Friday' isn't a deadline.
からに isn't grammatical.
Nouns need の before まえ: 金曜日のまえに.
questions.translation: Please give me your answer by Friday.

questions.prompt: （I bought it at the airport before leaving.）{日本|にほん}へ（　）とき、{空港|くうこう}でカメラを{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: The purchase happened **before arriving** → dictionary form: **行くとき**.
notes: The て-form can't modify とき.
The ます-stem can't modify とき.
行ったとき = after arriving in Japan — but the airport is at home, before the trip.
questions.translation: When I was going to Japan, I bought a camera at the airport.

questions.prompt: {日本|にほん}へ（　）とき、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りました。
questions.explanation: Climbing Fuji happened **in Japan, after arriving** → **行ったとき**.
notes: 行くとき = on the way / before arriving — you can't climb Fuji before you're in Japan.
The て-form can't modify とき.
The ます-stem can't modify とき.
questions.translation: When I went to Japan, I climbed Mt. Fuji.

questions.prompt: {暇|ひま}（　）とき、{何|なに}をしますか。
notes: に makes an adverb.
の is for nouns (子供のとき); 暇 is a な-adjective.
だ can't modify a noun like とき.
questions.translation: What do you do when you're free?

questions.prompt: {歩|ある}き（　）スマホを{見|み}ないでください。
notes: 歩きないで isn't a form (歩かないで).
歩きましょう ends a sentence.
ながらに is a fixed literary form (生まれながらに) — not 'while doing'.
questions.translation: Please don't look at your phone while walking.

questions.prompt: テレビを（　）ながら、ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます。
questions.explanation: ながら attaches to the **ます-stem**: 見ながら.
notes: The dictionary form doesn't take ながら.
The past form doesn't take ながら.
The て-form doesn't take ながら.

options: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}きながら{走|はし}ります。
コーヒーを{飲|の}みながら{話|はな}しましょう。
{私|わたし}が{歌|うた}いながら、{妹|いもうと}がピアノを{弾|ひ}きます。
{彼|かれ}は{笑|わら}いながら{答|こた}えました。
questions.explanation: ながら needs **one subject** for both actions. Two people → 私が歌っている間に / 私が歌うとき.
notes: Natural — one person does both.
Natural — the same people do both.
Natural — he laughed and answered.

questions.prompt: このバスは10{分|ぷん}（　）{来|き}ます。
notes: ずつ means 'each' (三つずつ) — not intervals.
までに = by — 'comes by 10 minutes' makes no sense.
ごろ is for points in time, not durations.

questions.prompt: What does 「{一日|いちにち}おきに{運動|うんどう}します」 mean?
questions.explanation: 一日**おき** = with one day skipped in between → every other day.
notes: For one day is 一日だけ.
Every day is 毎日 / 一日ごとに.
Once a day is 一日に一回.

questions.prompt: この{薬|くすり}は6{時間|じかん}（　）{飲|の}んでください。
notes: 6時間までに = by 6 hours — not repeating.
ずつ = 'each' — not an interval.
6時間あいだ isn't grammatical (6時間の間).
questions.translation: Please take this medicine every 6 hours.
